slides.heading: Lru Cache
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Lru Cache, a very hard linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: InsertKeyValuePair, getValueFromKey (null if missing) and getMostRecentKey, evicting the least recently used key at capacity.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. InsertKeyValuePair, getValueFromKey (null if missing) and getMostRecentKey, evicting the least recently used key at capacity. Hash map plus doubly linked list.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A hash map for lookup plus a doubly linked list for recency order gives constant-time operations.
slides.narration: A hash map for lookup plus a doubly linked list for recency order gives constant-time operations.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: List with linear search → O(n) ops
Hash map + doubly linked list → O(1) all ops
slides.narration: A list needs a scan to find and move keys. A hash map pointing into a doubly linked list gives constant-time lookup, move-to-front and eviction.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Move accessed nodes to the head
4. Most recent key is the head
slides.narration: Step by step. First, map keys to nodes. Second, move accessed nodes to the head. Third, evict the tail at capacity. Fourth, most recent key is the head.

slides.heading: Java solution (1/2)
slides.narration: Insert updates and moves an existing node, otherwise evicts the tail's previous node if full and adds a new node at the front. Get moves the node to the front and returns its value.

slides.heading: Java solution (2/2)
slides.narration: Insert updates and moves an existing node, otherwise evicts the tail's previous node if full and adds a new node at the front. Get moves the node to the front and returns its value.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is constant per op. Space is O of capacity.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Update existing key moves it to front
slides.narration: Updating an existing key also refreshes it.

slides.narration: Java's linked hash map can do this with access order.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A hash map for lookup plus a doubly linked list for recency order gives constant-time operations.
slides.narration: To recap Lru Cache: A hash map for lookup plus a doubly linked list for recency order gives constant-time operations. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
